PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Cloud infrastructure and platform engineer with 10 years of experience designing, building and operating infrastructure, including six years running Kubernetes platforms on AWS. Strong hands-on experience with Terraform and AWS, and a track record of leading platform initiatives from proposal through production. Builds reliable, observable platforms and self-service infrastructure that help engineering teams deliver services safely and efficiently.

CORE SKILLS
Cloud infrastructure design and operation: AWS (EKS, EC2, VPC, IAM, RDS, S3, SQS, Route 53, CloudFront), Kubernetes, Linux
Infrastructure as code: Terraform, Atlantis, Crossplane, Puppet
Platform engineering: Argo CD, Helm, Kustomize, Karpenter, GitHub Actions
Reliability and observability: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Alertmanager, OpenTelemetry, SLOs and error budgets, incident management
Programming and testing: Go, Python, Bash, k6

EXPERIENCE

Senior Platform Engineer | Tallybrook Ltd (B2B accounting SaaS)
Manchester / remote | Apr 2022 – Present
- Technical lead for a five-person platform team operating an AWS EKS platform across eight clusters and three regions, supporting approximately 350 services.
- Designed and built an internal developer platform with Go and Python service templates, Argo CD GitOps, and Crossplane self-service for RDS, SQS and S3. Adopted by all 14 product teams; reduced new-service time to production from approximately two weeks to under one day.
- Led an SLO programme for the 20 most critical services, introducing error budgets and burn-rate alerts with product leadership; reduced on-call pages per week by approximately 60%.
- Migrated node provisioning from managed node groups and Cluster Autoscaler to Karpenter, using Spot instances for stateless workloads with interruption handling. Reduced EC2 spend by 38% (approximately £410,000 per year).
- Participate in the incident commander rotation and established the incident and post-mortem process.

Site Reliability Engineer | Brightwater Games
Leeds | Jan 2019 – Mar 2022
- Operated AWS game-backend infrastructure using EC2, ECS and later EKS for titles with up to 1.2 million daily active players.
- Managed AWS infrastructure as code with approximately 40 Terraform modules and Atlantis plan/apply workflows on pull requests.
- Replaced a noisy Nagios setup with a Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager and Loki observability stack.
- Used k6 load tests and capacity planning to prepare launches, including testing scenarios with 300,000 concurrent players and identifying a connection-pool limit before launch.

Linux Systems Engineer | Pennine Hosting
Sheffield | Jul 2016 – Dec 2018
- Managed approximately 600 Linux servers for hosting customers using Puppet configuration management.
- Automated operational tasks with Bash and Python and provided on-call support for customer incidents.

SELECTED PROJECT
Kubernetes cleanup operator | Open source side project | 2024
- Built a Go Kubernetes controller using controller-runtime to delete expired preview namespaces; the project has approximately 120 GitHub stars.

LEADERSHIP & KNOWLEDGE SHARING
- Spoke at a UK DevOps meetup in 2024 on “SLOs that product managers care about”.
- Mentored three engineers transitioning from backend development into SRE.

EDUCATION
BSc Computer Science | University of the North Moors | 2016

Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) | 2021; renewed 2024
AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional | 2023

LANGUAGES
English (native) | Urdu (conversational)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, polished CV with a clear senior platform/SRE profile, consistent chronology, credible metrics, and good evidence of ownership. The strongest content is the internal developer platform, EKS operations, SLO programme, cost reduction, and high-scale load-testing work. Bullets are concise and outcome-focused, and the document is professionally structured. The main content weakness is that a few statements are broader than the supporting candidate information, and the CV does not explicitly frame its existing AWS networking and infrastructure experience in the system-design language used by the advert.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses conventional headings, plain text, standard date formats, readable bullets, and searchable technology names. It should parse well and has a high AI-screening probability for AWS, Kubernetes, Terraform, Linux, observability, reliability, and platform-engineering searches. Screening strength will be lower for this specific advert because Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, security awareness, and system design are not explicitly demonstrated. These are substantive evidence gaps rather than keywords that should be added without support. AWS services such as VPC and IAM are present, which provides useful adjacent signals.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns strongly with hands-on AWS infrastructure operation, Terraform, platform engineering, reliability, technical leadership, stakeholder collaboration with product leadership, Linux, and analytical capacity planning. The internal developer platform and self-service work are especially relevant to supporting backend developers and creating approachable operational paths. The CV is less aligned with the advert's secure train-to-cloud communication scope: there is no evidence of Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, IoT/vehicle/remote-device integration, or JVM development. It also does not explicitly describe formal system-design or network-design work, although the AWS, EKS, VPC, IAM, and platform-design experience is relevant adjacent evidence. The CV demonstrates collaborative leadership through platform-team leadership, product-leadership alignment, mentoring, and knowledge sharing, which fits the company's engineering-led and ownership-oriented culture.

This preserves the leadership claim without asserting proposal ownership that is not stated in the original candidate information.

MINOR, HIGH-VALUE TARGETING: In the Professional Summary, revise the opening to use the advert's supported terminology more directly: "Cloud infrastructure and platform engineer with 10 years of hands-on infrastructure engineering and cloud environment operation, including six years running Kubernetes platforms on AWS." Keep the existing sentences about reliable, observable platforms and self-service infrastructure after this opening.

Retain the existing Go, Python, Argo CD, Crossplane, adoption, and time-to-production details.

NADIA BRENNAN-AZIZ
Senior Cloud Infrastructure / Platform Engineer
Manchester, United Kingdom | nadia.brennanaziz@example.com | +44 7700 900909

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Cloud infrastructure and platform engineer with 10 years in infrastructure engineering, including six years running Kubernetes platforms on AWS, and experience with platform system design. Strong hands-on experience with Terraform and AWS, with a track record of leading platform initiatives, designing self-service infrastructure, and taking platform improvements into production, including a Karpenter migration that reduced EC2 spend by 38%, while building reliable, observable platforms that help engineering teams deliver services safely and efficiently.

LANGUAGES
English (native) | Urdu (conversational)

TECHNICAL TOOLKIT
Cloud infrastructure design and operation: AWS (EKS, EC2, VPC, IAM, RDS, S3, SQS, Route 53, CloudFront), Kubernetes, Linux
Infrastructure as code: Terraform, Atlantis, Crossplane, Puppet
Platform engineering: Argo CD, Helm, Kustomize, Karpenter, GitHub Actions
Reliability and observability: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Alertmanager, OpenTelemetry, SLOs and error budgets, incident management
Programming and testing: Go, Python, Bash, k6

EXPERIENCE

Senior Platform Engineer | Tallybrook Ltd (B2B accounting SaaS)
Manchester, United Kingdom / remote | Apr 2022 – Present
- Technical lead for a five-person platform team, operating and improving an AWS EKS platform across eight clusters and three regions, supporting approximately 350 services. Participate in the incident commander rotation and established the incident and post-mortem process.
- Designed and built an internal developer platform and self-service cloud infrastructure with Go and Python service templates, Argo CD GitOps, and Crossplane self-service for RDS, SQS and S3. Adopted by all 14 product teams; reduced new-service time to production from approximately two weeks to under one day.
- Led an SLO programme for the 20 most critical services, agreeing error-budget policy with product leadership and introducing burn-rate alerts; reduced on-call pages per week by approximately 60%.
- Migrated node provisioning from managed node groups and Cluster Autoscaler to Karpenter, using Spot instances for stateless workloads with interruption handling. Reduced EC2 spend by 38% (approximately £410,000 per year).

Site Reliability Engineer | Brightwater Games
Leeds | Jan 2019 – Mar 2022
- Operated AWS game-backend infrastructure using EC2, ECS and later EKS for titles with up to 1.2 million daily active players.
- Managed AWS infrastructure as code with approximately 40 Terraform modules and Atlantis plan/apply workflows on pull requests.
- Replaced a noisy Nagios setup with a Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager and Loki observability stack.
- Used k6 load tests and capacity planning to prepare launches, including simulations of 300,000 concurrent players; identified a connection-pool limit before launch and enabled it to be addressed before release.

SELECTED PROJECT
Kubernetes cleanup operator | Open source side project | 2024
- Built a Go Kubernetes controller with controller-runtime to delete expired preview namespaces; the project has approximately 120 GitHub stars.

LEADERSHIP & KNOWLEDGE SHARING
- Spoke at a UK DevOps meetup in 2024 on “SLOs that product managers care about”.
- Mentored three engineers transitioning from backend development into SRE.

EDUCATION
BSc Computer Science | University of the North Moors | 2016

CERTIFICATIONS
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) | 2021; renewed 2024
AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional | 2023

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, polished CV with a clear senior platform-engineering profile, strong quantified achievements, and an effective progression from infrastructure operations to technical leadership. The structure is easy to scan, and the strongest accomplishments are well prioritised: internal developer platform adoption, reduced time to production, lower on-call volume, and £410,000 annual EC2 savings. The four-bullet limit is respected for each listed role. Removing the earlier Linux Systems Engineer role reduces evidence of total career history, but this was an explicit instruction and the remaining experience is coherent. The main content weakness is that the CV does not explicitly demonstrate networking, TLS/mTLS, or practical security work required by this particular role; the candidate material also does not provide evidence for those areas, so they are candidate gaps rather than rewrite defects.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-friendly: conventional headings, plain text formatting, standard job titles, clear dates, and strong keyword coverage for AWS, EKS, Kubernetes, Terraform, Linux, Go, Python, observability, SLOs, GitOps, and incident management. The Technical Toolkit is well organised and uses searchable technology names. AI screening probability is high for general AWS platform, Kubernetes, SRE, and internal developer platform roles. For this advertisement, screening probability is reduced by the absence of Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, and explicit security terminology. These are not appropriate to add because they are not supported by the candidate information. The CV could, however, make its existing AWS networking, IAM, infrastructure design, stakeholder leadership, and analytical evidence more explicit.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns very well with the hands-on infrastructure, AWS, Terraform, cloud operation, platform reliability, observability, technical leadership, analytical thinking, and communication aspects of the role. It also supports Corvale's engineering-led and ownership-oriented culture through evidence of leading a platform team, creating self-service systems adopted by product teams, agreeing error-budget policy with product leadership, mentoring engineers, and taking improvements into production. Alignment is weaker for Terragrunt, mTLS/SSL/TLS, certificate management, practical security, and train-to-cloud or remote-device integration. The candidate also has no stated IoT/automotive experience and no JVM background. These are genuine profile gaps and should not be presented as CV defects or addressed by inventing experience.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, concise, professionally structured CV with clear progression from SRE to senior platform engineering. Quantified outcomes such as the 38% EC2 cost reduction, 60% reduction in on-call pages, adoption by all 14 product teams, and reduction in deployment time make the impact credible and easy to assess. The document also demonstrates technical leadership without overstating formal people-management responsibility. One minor content limitation is that the summary's phrase "experience with platform system design" is somewhat vague compared with the stronger architecture and platform-delivery evidence shown in the experience section.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses standard section headings, simple text formatting, chronological experience, conventional date formats, and keyword-rich descriptions. AWS, EKS, Terraform, Kubernetes, Linux, IAM, networking-related AWS services, observability, incident management, Go, Python, and platform engineering terms should parse well. Screening will be weaker for exact terms that are absent from both the CV and the candidate material, particularly Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, and IoT or remote-device integration. These are candidate-profile gaps rather than formatting defects and should not be added without truthful supporting evidence. The CV could use the job's exact supported wording around cloud environment design and operation and stakeholder-facing technical leadership more prominently.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns strongly with hands-on AWS infrastructure operation, cloud platform engineering, Terraform, Kubernetes, Linux, observability, reliability, system/platform design, technical leadership, analytical problem-solving, and clear communication. The strongest evidence includes operation of eight EKS clusters across three regions, approximately 350 services, Terraform and Atlantis workflows, the internal developer platform, SLO and error-budget work agreed with product leadership, and measurable cost and reliability improvements. The candidate's meetup talk and mentoring also support communication and knowledge-sharing. The material does not demonstrate Terragrunt, mTLS or SSL/TLS, certificate management, explicit practical security work, IoT/automotive/remote-device integration, or JVM-based backend development. The candidate has Linux experience and AWS EC2 experience, which provides a reasonable match for the Linux and virtual-machine nice-to-have, although virtual machines are not named explicitly. Overall, this is a convincing match for the platform and cloud infrastructure scope, with the main limitations being specialized fleet-connectivity security and remote-device experience.
